KorTTY terminal-effect plugins are Java KTPH000 plugins that can change the appearance and runtime behavior of a terminal session. They are trusted local code that runs inside the KorTTY JVM and integrate through a clean SPI interface.
Apply terminal appearance values such as font, foreground/background colors, cursor color, and cursor style
Add JavaFX overlay nodes above the terminal area (for example scanlines, noise, vignettes, or line highlights)
Wrap the SithTermFX KTPH000 to observe, pace, or transform terminal output before the terminal emulator receives it
React to the user-selected terminal-effect animation speed
Provide an animated preview that the plugin manager shows for the selected plugin (optional KTPH000)
KorTTY ships eleven built-in effects as two bundled, exportable plugin JARs: the MOTHER reference implementation (KTPH000) and the effect pack (KTPH001) with ten themed effects.
ALIEN-style green CRT terminal appearance with paced line output.
Amber phosphor CRT monitor from the 90s with scanlines, glow, flicker and a rolling refresh band.
Classic C64 home computer look: light blue on blue with a chunky cursor and loader bars.
Cyberpunk neon look with glitch tears, RGB-split flickers and pulsing glow.
Green-on-black matrix style with a faint stream of falling glyphs.
Translucent sci-fi hologram with interference bands, HUD corner brackets and flicker.
Haunted monochrome terminal with a breathing vignette, static bursts and ghostly flashes.
Worn VHS tape playback with tracking noise, rolling distortion and a PLAY overlay.
Retro-80s synthwave palette with a glowing perspective grid on the horizon.
Tactical deep-space console with a slow radar sweep, faint blips and frame corners.
Sepia paper and ink noir look with per-character typewriter output pacing.

All built-in effects override the terminal appearance (font, colors, cursor) while active and draw their animation as a mouse-transparent canvas overlay. Typewriter Noir additionally wraps the connector to pace output character by character. Effect names are proper nouns and stay untranslated; descriptions are localized through the KTPH000 message keys with an English fallback.
Terminal-effect plugins are loaded by KTPH000 in this order:
Bundled plugin JARs listed by KTPH000
If two plugins expose the same plugin ID, the first one wins and later duplicates are ignored. This is intentional because connection settings persist the plugin ID.

External plugins are loaded from one JAR at a time with KorTTY's application classloader as parent. Dependencies that are already part of KorTTY can be used from that parent classloader. Dependencies that are not part of KorTTY are not discovered from adjacent files automatically; either avoid them or shade them into the plugin JAR.

Terminal-effect plugins are trusted local Java code. KorTTY does not sandbox imported JARs. A plugin runs inside the KorTTY JVM with the same local process permissions as KorTTY itself. Only import plugins from sources you trust.
Users manage terminal-effect plugins from KTPH000Plugins KTPH002 Terminal EffectsKTPH001.

The Terminal Effects manager window is resizable, so you can expand the plugin table and descriptions while keeping the live preview visible. If tool windows are configured to open as tabs, the manager instead uses the available main-window tab area.
The dialog shows the loaded plugin list with:

Next to the table, a preview panel plays a live animated preview of the selected plugin (a small fake terminal in the effect's colors with the effect overlay on top). If a plugin does not implement KTPH000, the panel shows a placeholder text instead. The preview stops when the selection changes, the global terminal-effects switch is turned off, or the dialog closes.
Import an external KTPH000 plugin, which KorTTY copies to KTPH001
Export plugins that have a source JAR (the bundled MOTHER and effect-pack JARs are exportable)

Users select effects per terminal session from the terminal context menu or KTPH003View KTPH005 Terminal EffectKTPH004. Saved connections can also store the selected effect and animation speed through Quick Connect and Connection Manager. The speed slider covers KTPH000 through KTPH001; the numeric field accepts values up to KTPH002.
The public SPI lives under KTPH000.
Implement KTPH000 as the KTPH001 entry point.
KTPH000 must be stable because connection settings and disabled-plugin state persist it
Valid IDs match the regex KTPH000
KTPH000 is shown in the plugin-management table and should be one short sentence
The provider class must be loadable by KTPH000; use a public class with a public no-argument constructor
KTPH000 is optional; returning KTPH001 (the default) shows a placeholder in the plugin manager
KTPH000 returns one KTPH001 per terminal tab/effect activation.
Decorate connectors in KTPH000 when output pacing or filtering is needed
Remove listeners, stop timelines, unbind properties, and release references in KTPH000
KTPH000 must be idempotent. It can be called when a user disables the effect, switches effects, closes a tab, or reloads plugins.
KTPH000 exposes the active terminal environment:
A JavaFX KTPH000 above the terminal area; add overlay nodes here
Current SithTermFX widgets for the terminal view; split terminals can have more than one widget
Restores the baseline appearance captured before the effect was activated
JavaFX scene-graph changes must run on the JavaFX application thread. If a callback can arrive from a terminal worker thread, use KTPH000 for overlay or UI updates.
KTPH000 is a record with nullable fields:
Use only the fields your effect needs. KTPH000 leaves the current value unchanged.

The current implementation passes color values as strings, for example KTPH000. Cursor style is also a string; the MOTHER effect uses KTPH001. Reuse values already accepted by KorTTY's terminal settings instead of inventing new names.
KTPH000 returns the animated preview shown in the plugin manager:
One preview instance backs one displayed preview; the caller requests KTPH000 once, calls KTPH001 after attaching it, and KTPH002 before discarding it
Do not construct JavaFX objects before KTPH000 is called, so plugin metadata stays usable without a running JavaFX toolkit
KTPH000 must stop all timelines and release animation resources

KTPH000 (same package) is a reusable implementation used by all built-in effects: a 360x220 fake terminal with configurable colors, fake shell lines, a blinking cursor, and an optional effect overlay canvas on top. Its builder collects plain data only and creates JavaFX nodes lazily in KTPH001.
If a plugin wraps a connector, implement KTPH000 and delegate all KTPH001 methods to the wrapped connector unless the effect intentionally changes that method.

KorTTY uses this marker to unwrap effect connectors before applying another wrapper or before accessing the underlying SSH connector. Without it, reconnect, drag/drop upload, AI-agent current-directory tracking, or future connector-level features can see the wrong connector.
This example changes appearance only. It does not need an overlay or connector wrapper.

This repository does not currently define a separately published terminal-effect SDK artifact. Plugin code must compile against the KorTTY classes that contain KTPH000 and against the same public libraries the plugin directly imports, such as SithTermFX or JavaFX.
For development inside this repository, use the MOTHER source-set pattern in KTPH000:
Put plugin sources under a separate source set
Include KTPH000 and KTPH001 in that source set's compile classpath
Package only the plugin source-set output into a plugin JAR
Include the ServiceLoader descriptor in the plugin JAR
The MOTHER and effect-pack tasks are the concrete, tested examples:

A single plugin JAR can register several effects: the effect pack lists all ten provider classes in one ServiceLoader descriptor. Bundled JARs must additionally be listed in KTPH000, otherwise they are never extracted and loaded.

For an out-of-tree plugin, the same rule applies: produce one importable JAR containing your plugin classes and KTPH000. If you use libraries that KorTTY does not already ship, shade them into that same JAR or remove that dependency.
Use KTPH000 only when the effect must observe, pace, or transform terminal I/O. Pure visual overlays and appearance changes should avoid wrapping connectors.
Delegate KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002, KTPH003, KTPH004, KTPH005, and KTPH006 unless the effect has a specific reason to change them
Handle KTPH000 by restoring the interrupt flag and converting to an appropriate checked exception where the KTPH001 method requires it
Avoid unbounded buffering because terminal output can be large
Avoid delaying control sequences such as ANSI CSI/OSC commands unless the effect intentionally changes terminal protocol behavior
Implement KTPH000 so KorTTY can unwrap to the real connector

MOTHER's KTPH000 is the current reference for output pacing. It splits terminal output into immediate control sequences and paced visible characters, uses the user animation speed, and bypasses pacing for high-volume output to keep the terminal responsive.
Overlays should be JavaFX nodes added to KTPH000.
Set KTPH000 so the terminal keeps receiving mouse input
Set KTPH000 if the overlay should not affect layout
Bind width and height to the overlay root
Stop timelines/animations and unbind properties in KTPH000
Keep drawing cheap enough for repeated repainting
Remove the overlay node from KTPH000 on shutdown

Release the canvas backing store while the tab is in the background: a full-window canvas texture per hidden tab can exhaust the Prism texture pool once several effect tabs are open, which crashes rendering. All built-in effects (MOTHER and the effect pack) unbind and shrink their overlay canvas to 0x0 while it is not visible in the scene and rebind when the tab is shown again
For split terminals, decide whether the overlay should cover the full terminal tab or track individual SithTermFX widgets. KTPH000 can return more than one widget.
Animation speed is a shared user setting for terminal effects:
Invalid, non-finite, or non-positive values normalize to KTPH000
Use KTPH000 when computing effect timing. The convention used by MOTHER is:
Do not persist a separate speed value inside the plugin. KorTTY stores the connection/session speed and passes the normalized value through KTPH000.
The user selects a KTPH000 in KTPH001Plugins KTPH003 Terminal Effects KTPH004 Import...KTPH002
The plugin manager reloads plugins immediately
A plugin is exportable when it was loaded from a real source JAR
Bundled plugins are exportable because KorTTY copies their bundled JARs to KTPH000 before loading them
Exporting one of the ten effect-pack effects exports the whole KTPH000, because the JAR is the export unit
Application-classpath plugins without a source JAR are not exportable
Disabled plugin IDs are stored in KTPH000
Saved connections and restored sessions store the selected terminal-effect plugin ID and animation speed
If a saved plugin ID is unavailable or disabled, KorTTY cannot activate it and logs the issue
Use a stable lowercase plugin ID matching KTPH000
Keep KTPH000 and KTPH001 non-empty and user-readable
Include exactly one ServiceLoader descriptor for every provider class
Keep JavaFX mutations on the JavaFX application thread
Make KTPH000 safe to call multiple times
Remove listeners, timelines, bindings, and overlay nodes in KTPH000
Avoid blocking the JavaFX application thread
Keep connector wrappers transparent and implement KTPH000
Avoid logging secrets or raw terminal output unless the user explicitly chose that behavior
Test with fast output, large output, ANSI color output, split terminals, reconnect, plugin disable/enable, and application shutdown
Confirm all built-in plugins appear with name and description
Select a row and confirm the animated preview plays next to the table
Export one and inspect the exported JAR with KTPH000
Import the exported JAR into a clean KorTTY config or another build
The KTPH000 Gradle task renders every built-in preview and the manager dialog headless into KTPH001 for a quick offline check.
Activate the effect from the terminal context menu or KTPH000View KTPH002 Terminal EffectKTPH001
Select it in Quick Connect and in a saved Connection Manager entry
Change animation speed with the slider and with the numeric field
Run commands that produce slow, fast, colored, and large output
Reconnect the tab and close it
Check KTPH000 for plugin loading warnings, duplicate IDs, invalid providers, or stop/cleanup errors
